one_line.text: A self-published writer who turns ideas from philosophy, spirituality and psychology into short, accessible books about overthinking and inner peace.

biography.text: Nguyen says his work grew from his own experience of overthinking and a wish to help readers find peace. He first published Don't Believe Everything You Think independently in 2022; its online word of mouth led to bestseller status and a later expanded edition from Authors Equity. His publisher says his work has reached millions of readers and more than forty languages. Public biographies focus on his writing and teaching rather than his early life.

background.text: Nguyen describes himself as a writer, teacher and speaker. He draws openly from philosophy, spirituality and psychology, but writes in plain, personal language rather than as a scholar or clinician. In 2025 he was named a NAMI ambassador.

expertise.text: His demonstrated expertise is in explaining contemplative self-help ideas to a broad audience. Independent coverage reports no formal training in psychology or philosophy, so claims about mental health should be judged as personal guidance, not clinical authority.

perspective_and_limits.text: Nguyen writes as someone sharing what helped him. That gives his work warmth and immediacy, but it also encourages broad conclusions from personal experience. His central thought-distancing move has recognised relatives in contemplative practice and psychology; the book does not provide evidence proportionate to its claim about all psychological suffering.
